subject.title: Telegram detached subagents can run silently without liveness or terminal notification

question: Should Telegram-visible detached-subagent liveness and terminal delivery be implemented as its own channel-facing work item, or folded into the broader session/task activity and owner-session delivery work first?
rationale: The implementation boundary spans Telegram UX, core subagent/task state, heartbeat wake routing, possible configuration, and open partial fixes, so automation should not choose the public delivery policy alone.

options.title: Keep Telegram Slice
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical Telegram-visible liveness and terminal-notification slice, while linking the active parent-settle and raw-output PRs as partial dependencies.

options.title: Fold Into Generic Activity Work
options.body: Move the Telegram evidence into the broader session activity/watchdog issues and require the channel UI to consume that shared contract later.

options.title: Wait For Partial PRs
options.body: Defer this issue until the open parent-settle, raw-output, and owner-session delivery PRs land, then re-evaluate the remaining Telegram liveness gap.

recommendation.title: Keep Telegram Slice
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical Telegram-visible liveness and terminal-notification slice, while linking the active parent-settle and raw-output PRs as partial dependencies.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest available history across subagent lifecycle, announce, task, and current Telegram/status/heartbeat surfaces.
